source.title: Causally Grounded Mechanistic Interpretability for LLMs with Faithful Natural-Language Explanations

page_placements.theme: Dataset-average circuits incompletely describe individual prompts

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: It tests IOI-related circuit contributions in GPT-2 Small using activation patching and adapted sufficiency/comprehensiveness metrics, but evaluates a top-six-head circuit rather than reproducing the original 26-head circuit and its full criteria.
record.gate_note: The study reports patching-derived contributions for six heads, top-six circuit coverage, and sufficiency/comprehensiveness results. It also reports an added-head F1 result and prompt-level comprehensiveness distribution. The 100% IOI accuracy is not a circuit result. Attention and random baselines compare faithfulness scores, not recovery of the claimed circuit; explanation-quality and confidence results do not test the listed circuit versions.
record.test_reason: The main aim is an explanation pipeline that treats the IOI circuit as ground truth. It still reports its own activation-patching results on GPT-2 small IOI. These bear narrowly on V1 (whether Wang's name-mover and S-inhibition heads are the top causal heads) and weakly on V5 (how much a small head set explains, and how that varies by prompt). It never evaluates the full 26-head circuit. Its corruption swaps name positions, unlike the original ABC distribution.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors also state the six-head result is consistent with Wang et al. Their main conclusions concern explanations: LLM-generated explanations beat templates by 66% on quality, and confidence does not predict faithfulness (r = 0.009).
record.recipe_differences: Uses activation patching on GPT-2 Small IOI, but identifies a top-six set and evaluates it with adapted ERASER sufficiency and comprehensiveness metrics rather than testing the original 26-head circuit and its full criteria.
record.method_sensitivity: Comprehensiveness varies across prompts: 34% of cases are below 15%, 30% are 15–25%, and 36% are above 25%. Outcomes are not reported separately by template.

fits_no_version.finding: A top-six head set from the IOI circuit gives 22% comprehensiveness on average. Comprehensiveness varies widely across prompts, and L10H10 appears in 82% of low-comprehensiveness cases.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A small top-k subset of the IOI circuit, chosen by dataset-average patching, accounts for only part of the IOI behaviour, and how much it accounts for varies strongly by prompt.

record.code_released: GitHub code repository will be made public after thesis submission; no URL stated.
record.problems: The authors note that the evaluation uses one task and one model, only 50 prompts, a fixed top-six circuit, and dataset-average rather than instance-specific head importance. They do not evaluate human utility of explanations.

untested.parts: Full 26-head, 7-class circuit; duplicate-token, induction, previous-token and negative heads; the original faithfulness, completeness and minimality criteria.
No ablation of the main name movers followed by a measure of compensation.
Only GPT-2 small; no other models, sizes, checkpoints or tasks.
No comparison with other circuit-discovery methods or ablation types. The attention and random baselines compare explanation faithfulness, not circuit recovery.
Effect of ablation type and metric choice; how much of the behaviour the full circuit explains.
Name orders, separate per-template results, and prompts with more names.

missing.what: L10H10 (a backup name mover in Wang et al.) appears in 82% of low-comprehensiveness failure cases.

record.verdict_notes: The paper is an MSc-thesis preprint whose focus is natural-language explanation, with the circuit used as ground truth; it could arguably be T4. The reader's V1 limits_scope label was dropped: low coverage and low comprehensiveness for a six-head subset are expected under the 26-head V1 and do not qualify it. The V5 supports label was dropped because R9 and R11 measure a subset, not the circuit, so they are recorded under fits_no_version. The sufficiency formula and the 100% value appear inconsistent with the 61.4% summed coverage. No code is available.

versions.untested_parts: The full 26-head, 7-class circuit and its complete set of roles are not evaluated. The reported head roles are assigned based on Wang et al. (2023); the study does not test the original circuit's faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria as a whole.
The study does not ablate the main name-mover heads and test whether other heads take over.
Only GPT-2 Small is evaluated; other models, sizes, checkpoints, and reuse across tasks are not tested.
The study does not compare circuit-finding methods or ablation types to determine whether they recover the same circuit.
It reports variation in comprehensiveness across prompts, but does not compare alternative ablation types or faithfulness metrics, or separately report outcomes by prompt template.

The evaluation uses two templates, but results are aggregated and do not establish that the same components carry IOI separately across templates. Other name orders and prompts with more names are not tested.

rows.subject: GPT-2 Small
rows.operation_detail: Aggregate effect recovery of the top six heads
rows.note: The paper says the remaining 38.6% is distributed across other heads.
rows.check: The coverage figure comes from six heads out of the 26-head circuit, so it cannot show V1's completeness. The 61.4% is a sum of per-head effect recoveries, not a joint patch. It also conflicts with the reported 100% sufficiency.

rows.subject: GPT-2 Small
rows.operation_detail: Evaluate sufficiency of the cited top-six heads
rows.note: This is the study's adapted circuit-level sufficiency measure, not a test of the full 26-head circuit.
rows.check: Sufficiency of 100% ± 0.0% is internally inconsistent with 61.4% summed coverage, and the formula is garbled in the text. It is not V1's faithfulness criterion, and the value is hard to interpret.

rows.subject: GPT-2 Small
rows.operation_detail: Ablate the cited top-six heads and measure comprehensiveness
rows.note: The authors interpret this as only partial degradation when the cited heads are ablated.
rows.check: The ablation removes only 6 of the 26 heads. A 22% drop is expected under V1, given that backup name movers are left intact, so it can neither confirm nor refute V1 completeness. The ablation type is not stated.

source_check.correct: Comprehensiveness is 22.0% ± 17.3% (mean ± standard deviation); its reference is clean logit difference, averaging 3.36. The intervention concerns the selected six heads.
source_check.problem: The clean reference is stated; this subset ablation cannot establish completeness of the original 26-head circuit.

rows.subject: GPT-2 Small
rows.operation_detail: Add L10H10 to the top-six circuit
rows.note: The authors describe the added head as redundant; this is a single addition test, not a full minimality evaluation.
rows.check: Adding L10H10, a backup name mover in Wang et al., lowers the study's F1 from 36.0% to 34.4%. F1 is a harmonic mean of the adapted metrics, not a minimality test. No uncertainty is given for a 1.6-point change.

labels.label: supports
labels.condition: GPT-2 small, 50 IOI prompts (2 templates), per-head activation patching with name-swap corruption
labels.reason: R1–R6 show causal contributions from named name-mover, backup name-mover and S-inhibition heads, with L9H9 largest. Support is limited to these components; the 26-head inventory, seven classes, completeness and minimality remain untested.

relation.reason: Its own activation-patching results bear narrowly on the causal involvement of named IOI heads, despite using the established circuit as ground truth for explanation generation.

tranche.reason: The study reports its own IOI head-patching results and evaluates a selected six-head set using adapted ERASER metrics, providing a different evaluation of the circuit question.

source_check.notes: Table 1 itself labels L10H0 Backup Name Mover; the asserted correction to Wang's classification requires another source. Ablation implementation is unspecified, and code is promised after thesis submission rather than documented as publicly available.

statements.correction: GPT-2 Small; 50 IOI prompts; 25 name pairs × 2 templates; name-position-swap corruption; nonzero patching effects for named name-mover and S-inhibition heads; patching token position unspecified; original 26-head circuit not reconstructed.
statements.problem: The contribution claim is supported, but this study does not specify END/final-token placement of the activation-patching intervention. Numerical results attributed to the other studies are outside this check.

reader_labels.reason: The six heads cover 61.4% and have 22.0% comprehensiveness, so these results do not establish a complete circuit accounting for the behavior (R7, R9).

reader_labels.label: supports
